angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 400,723 km at 134.18 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.4529 +/- 0.0202 mas (same row, RUWE 1.21): 134.18 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.576 +/- 0.022 solar radii from Yalçinkaya et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-6223 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.209Y/abstract): 400,723 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.582 +/- 0.027 solar masses from Yalçinkaya et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-6223 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.209Y/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3895 +/- 44 K from Yalçinkaya et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6223 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.209Y/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Yalçinkaya et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6223 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.209Y/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-6223.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.682, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
